title: Lessons with Alphonse Picou in New Orleans
summary: Papa arranged a few lessons from Picou during Joe's summers at his sister's in New Orleans, but Roque and Fritz were his real teachers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: One thing I must do before we go any further, because we're going to come right back to St. Louis and Charlie Creath behind this... I've neglected to ask you where did Alphonse Picou come into all this? I know he taught you a lot of things.
Let's go back for a second.

Yeah. At one time, Picou, like I said, was a good friend of Papa's. People could talk Creole and French just like a Frenchman, and so could my Dad. And that's all they talked; they talked French together. And Picou, Papa asked him would he give me some lessons. Because Picou was half-assed famous, you see.
What was Picou doing in Baton Rouge?
He come there to play! Come there with some band.
A band out of New Orleans.

Oh yeah. I forget what band it was. Maybe ...(?)., you know. I can't remember all of the details of it. But I know every time he came to Baton Rouge, he used to come there. But Papa asked him one time, "Would you give him some lessons?" Because every summer I went to New Orleans, because I had my older sister who lived there -- she'd married a guy in New Orleans and lived there. And Picou would say, "Yeah, I'll give him some lessons." But Picou never really taught me anything. Because Picou never had that much time for me. Maybe I took about three lessons from him. I remember the first time he told me to come around his house there. He lived on Marais Street...
Yes. I went to my sister's to spend the summer.
So the lessons that you took with Picou, even though it was only three or four of them, whatever it was you said, were in New Orleans, not in Baton Rouge.

Not in Baton Rouge, no-no-no. He just came to Baton Rouge to play, then he went back to New Orleans. But my Papa used to go by his house in New Orleans sometimes, when Papa lived in New Orleans, to buy leather supplies. That's how all of those things tied in together.
Most people talk about Picou being your teacher. So he wasn't your teacher like Isadore Fritz or Manuel Roque was.

No-no, not really. Manuel Roque really, really was my teacher, and Fritz I admired... I liked Fritz a lot better, but Manuel Roque was my teacher. And I learned more from Fritz for the simple reason that I paid more attention to his playing and everything. Although Manuel Roque was a pretty good saxophone player, too. He played a C-melody saxophone.
